title: Richard Stallman and the GNU Project (1983)
explainer: On September 27, 1983, Richard Stallman announced the GNU Project with the explicit goal of building a complete operating system that anyone could run, study, modify, and redistribute - the founding act of what became the free and open-source software movement. Nearly every norm you'll meet reading and contributing to a real open-source codebase, from public source to open licenses to outside patches, descends from that one announcement.

title: Michael Fagan and the Invention of Formal Code Inspection (1976)
explainer: In a 1976 paper in the IBM Systems Journal, Michael Fagan described a formal process for groups to inspect code and design documents and catch defects close to where they were introduced - one of the earliest systematic descriptions of what is now called code review. The pull requests and review comments you'll practice in this lesson are a direct, informalized descendant of that process.
